patterns.note: Burden frames ("better off without me", "happier if I was gone"). Plain "better without me" is excluded: it is common about work.
First-person wish-to-be-dead frame.
"I feel like dying" is a common way to state passive ideation; illness uses also get a human look (recall first).
Not-waking-up wishes. Requires a wish/hope frame, "what if I didn't", or a sleep frame, so "I didn't wake up on time" does not match.
"Don't want to be here/live" needs "anymore" or the end of the sentence; "be alive" and "exist" match anywhere.

patterns.pattern: (?:(?<=\bi['’]m )|(?<=\bim )|(?<=\bi am )|(?<=\bi was )|(?<=\bi feel )|(?<=\bi felt )|(?<=\bbeen )|(?<=\bfeeling )|(?<=\bnot )|(?<=\bso )|(?<=\breally )|(?<=\bvery )|(?<=\bkinda )|(?<=\bpretty )|(?<=\bgetting )|(?<=\bget )|(?<=\bgot )|(?<=\bmore )|(?<=\bactively )|(?<=\bpassively )|(?<=\bsuper )|(?<=\bkind of )|(?<=\bhave )|(?<=\bhad )|(?<=\bhaving )|(?<=\bmy )|(?<!\bscreen for )(?<!\bscreening for )(?<=\bfor ))suicidal(?:\s+(?:thoughts?|feelings?|ideation|urges?|impulses?|thinking))?\b(?!\s+(?:patients?|people|clients?|teens?|youth|kids|students|individuals|persons?|callers?|squeeze|prevention)\b)
patterns.note: The bare word "suicidal" counts only after a first-person or state frame (SPEC §4 clarification). Frames are fixed-width lookbehinds so a negation such as "I'm not suicidal" stays outside the span and scopes over it.
Often flippant; idiom cues (an interjection such as "ugh") suppress the figurative use.
"I'd rather die than <chore>" is suppressed by idiom.rather_die_than.
Other reflexives also match so that third-party and question uses are kept as findings; the third_party and hypothetical cues set their level.
Bare "ending it" is ambiguous (relationships, meetings); it needs a thinking or intention frame and must not be followed by "with", "there", "on" and similar.
Overdose wording counts as an act; a distant past anchor turns it into history.
Method wording. Figurative "shoot myself in the foot" and "drowning myself in work" are excluded.
Needs an ideation frame ("picturing myself jumping off..."), so "kids jumping off the bridge into the lake" does not match.
Explicit preparation wording is crisis language on its own; the immediacy.* cues also flag it.
Self-injury verbs with a reflexive. Explicit accident contexts ("cut myself shaving", "hurt myself skiing", "burned myself on the stove") are excluded; "on purpose" is not.
Intransitive "cutting" is polysemous (costs, carbs, hair); it needs a habit frame and a self-harm continuation.
"I'm not safe at home" or "with him" signals risk from others (out of scope for v1) and is excluded.
Needs "like this", "anymore" or the end of the clause, so "I can't go on Friday" does not match.
First-person frame required: "the project is falling apart" does not match.
Needs a strong intensifier: plain "overwhelmed" is everyday work talk.
Fixed-width lookbehind frames keep "I'm not panicking" negatable (SPEC §4: negated distress is kept as a none finding).

Ambiguous first-person death words ("I'm dying", "I could just die", "I'm dead"). Usually figurative: idiom cues suppress the common uses, and what is left gets a human look at concern (recall first).
SRL lists "killing me" as a hazard term. Kept as a concern-level finding so idiom cues can mark it explicitly.
First-person "<feeling> to death" intensifiers; idiom.to_death suppresses the figurative ones.
Almost always figurative; idiom.death_of_me suppresses it.
Noun forms of a past attempt. Verb forms ("I tried to kill myself") are crisis patterns that a distant past anchor turns into history.
Timing cue. Raises immediacy only next to a non-negated crisis finding.
Lethal means. Never a finding on its own: it raises immediacy only next to a crisis finding (SPEC §4).
Preparation (NIMH warning signs: saying goodbye, giving things away, making a will, researching ways to die).

modifiers.note: Pseudo-negations ("not only", "not sure", "cannot") are excluded so they cannot soften a statement.
Covers "don't", "dont", "won't", "wouldnt" and similar. "can't" and "couldn't" express inability, not denial, and are not cues. Pseudo-negations ("don't know", "can't stop") are excluded.
"Never felt so..." intensifies rather than denies and is excluded.
"no" as a determiner ("no plan", "no intention of"). "No longer", "no one", "no point" carry crisis meaning and are excluded.
A third-person subject shortly before the finding, in the same clause.
"My <relation>" as the subject. Blocked when a first-person token follows it ("My family would be better off without me" stays self).
A non-first-person reflexive inside the finding ("cuts herself"). "themselves" in a question is left to the hypothetical cues.
A first-person token between a forward third-party cue and the end of the finding returns the statement to the writer ("Since she left I want to die").
"Is it bad that I want to die" is a disclosure, not a hypothetical, so "that" is not included.
Questions about procedure ("would you have to report it").
A reported screening question ("the nurse asked if I was having thoughts of...").
"How do I ..." is not included: a first-person question about one's own ideation stays crisis.
"What should I do if I want to die" is excluded: it is first-person help-seeking.

modifiers.subject: unknown
modifiers.note: A generic subject inside a question ("how do you know if someone is thinking about ending it?"). Sets subject "unknown".
Keeps "Do you think they'd be better off without me?" with the writer.
Weeks and days ago are recent (SPEC §4 clarification) and do not set past.
"When I was <age or life stage>". "When I was alone" is not an anchor. Present tense in the clause ("I'm in high school and...") cancels past.
"I'm used to" (habituation) is excluded.
"Last night/week" are recent and do not set past.
Present tense in the finding's clause ("after the divorce I want to die") cancels it: see past.block_present_tense.
"When my son died I wanted to die too." Present tense in the clause cancels it.
Refers back to the previous clause or sentence ("I wanted to die when my wife left, but that was a long time ago"), so it looks across boundaries into the same or the previous sentence.
"I have a history of self-harm" reports the past.
Recent past is present (SPEC §4 clarification): a recent or present anchor in the finding's own clause cancels past.
A present-tense first-person verb in the finding's clause means the statement is current, whatever anchor the sentence has.
A thing as the subject ("this commute is killing me"). Emotional subjects ("the depression is killing me") are excluded and stay concern.
"My manager is going to kill me" (being in trouble). "I wish someone would kill me" is excluded.
Past-tense "that joke killed me" cannot be literal for the writer; "it kills me to see her like this".
Effort hyperbole ("killing myself to finish the report"). "Killing myself to end the pain" does not match.
"Killed it at the pitch", "killing it on the sales floor".
Laughing slang ("im dead lmao").
"I could just die, this cake is amazing"; "I almost died when I saw the bill".
"Scared to death of what I might do" is not an idiom and is excluded.
"I'd rather die than sit through another all-hands" is figurative; "rather die than keep living like this" is not.
An apostrophe between letters ("I'm") does not close the quote, so "goes 'I want to die young'" works.
Reported media without quotation marks ("the song goes I want to die young").
The writer quoting their own thoughts or words ("I keep thinking 'I want to die'") is not reported speech.

boundaries.note: A contrast starts a new clause for every modifier, including the sentence-scoped ones (past, hypothetical).
"and (lately) I ..." starts a new first-person clause: "I tried in 2019 and lately I want to die again".
